before.decision: The claim cannot be proved with known mathematics. For irreducible Gamma (the only reading the setting allows) it is equivalent to finiteness of exceptional Maass cusp forms across the p-power level tower, which is open; Selberg's conjecture would imply it. For reducible Gamma it is false. The researcher must choose what this node states: (a) the provable uniform gap sup_{Z^0_+} s <= 1/2+7/64 (Kim-Sarnak), (b) an explicit hypothesis on Gamma, or (c) conditional on Selberg's conjecture. Details are in scratch/proof-draft.md.

The node statement is false as written, not ambiguous (scratch/proof-draft.md). (1) Gamma=SL_2(Z[1/p]), g_p=1, admissible bounded p-adic metric min(d_p,1): d_X((diag(p^k,p^-k),1),x_0) stays bounded while ht>=p^{2k}. (2) Doubling both metrics doubles d_X, so at most one metric scaling can satisfy it. (3) Conjugating Gamma by (h_inf,1) makes ht identically +inf. The researcher needs to choose a corrected statement. Proposal R2, proved in the draft: Gamma=SL_2(Z[1/p]), K_p=SL_2(Z_p); ht(Gamma(g_inf,g_p)) = y(delta_inf g_inf i) ≍ exp(hyperbolic distance in SL_2(Z)\H), i.e. d_X replaced by the fibre distance with g_p frozen. This is also what the Sobolev-embedding use and fog-2 need. Alternatively, restrict Gamma and fix specific metrics, but then the exponent only matches for one tuned normalisation.

No split. The statement is false as written: its p-adic factor nu_p(B_p(p^n))^{-1/2} Xi_p(a_n)^{kappa_p} is beaten by an L^2 lower bound (fog-10). For Gamma=SL_2(Z[1/p]), W=K_p, f a lifted Hecke-Maass form and T fixed, ||A_B f||_2 >> nu_p^{-1/2} infinitely often in n, while the claim forces an extra Xi_p(a_n)^{kappa_p}. The researcher must choose the intended p-adic factor. Likely intended: B_p(p^{2n}) with factor Xi_p(a_n)^{kappa_p}, proved by thickening. A split for that reading is drafted in scratch/decomposer/notes.md.
